correctness_confidence.basis: The full shared-panel reference is kept fixed. Maximizing expected conditional loss over count patterns before averaging provides the correct adaptive envelope. Group sampling is uniform given the chosen occupancy and realized panel.

rigor.basis: Uniform permutation covariances give the between-pair coefficient. The data analysis sums over every eligible subset and uses one parent event per strict contract. Percentile bootstrap inference is approximate and requires exchangeability.

novelty.basis: The original release already simulates uniform subpanels by size. Conditioning on occupancy, proving a worst-case minimum count and checking an adaptive sharp envelope against the full shared panel go beyond that baseline.

significance.basis: A simple policy distinction reverses empirical conclusions for two endpoints. The small mean margins and broad uncertainty restrict any practical recommendation for new contracts.

reproducibility.basis: The OSF archive hash, inclusion manifest, endpoint files, group keys, rounding checks, bootstrap seed and exact source version are recoverable. Individual calls are reused, without new model sampling.

summary: I took part in the analysis and writing. I examined all five pages of this revised PDF, its individual-contract replication and the model assessment prompt for this hash. The minimum sample counts have a clear finite-benchmark interpretation. Their favorable worst-policy mean coexists with positive losses on many contracts and with bootstrap intervals spanning zero. The inference is appropriately exploratory.
strengths: Direct pairing recovers the primary six-output effects to published precision.
Separating the contract-specific maximum from a population confidence bound resolves a potentially consequential interpretation error.
Published aggregates yield sufficient bounds without assuming identical panel size across contracts.
weaknesses: Post-hoc design choices and the small effects limit the interpretation of the bootstrap intervals.
Uniform permutation among named evidence groups is a substantive condition in a deployed system.
The implementation uses a small numerical tolerance for the count of strictly worse contracts; documenting that convention in the text would remove a minor ambiguity.
potential_errors: The largest conditional expected loss may require outcome knowledge. It is an envelope and cannot be treated as an implementable forecasting strategy.
The worst-policy benchmark mean is negative for all endpoints, yet the empirical 95 percent intervals do not establish a population gain.
Panel thinning after all six calls were collected does not measure inference-time savings.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact minima of three, one and three against complete shared-news forecasts, replicated by per-event subset enumeration under response-aware selection of unnamed group counts.
